key_insight: HIPE-2026 frames person–place relation extraction as a targeted multilingual evaluation over noisy historical texts, focusing on two pragmatic relation types (ever-at vs. contemporaneous location) to push semantic IE in diachronic, OCR-affected corpora.
problem_solved: Provides a standardized evaluation and benchmark for extracting accurate person–place associations from noisy, multilingual historical documents across time periods—addressing ambiguity, OCR errors, language variation, and temporality.
method: Curated multilingual, diachronic corpora with noisy historical and OCR-processed texts and annotated person–place relations.
Defined a two-label relation taxonomy: at (Has the person ever been at this place?) and isAt (Is the person located at the place around the text's timestamp?), with clear annotation guidelines.
Organized benchmark tasks, baseline systems, and multilingual evaluation metrics to compare accuracy and efficiency across languages and periods.
impact: Enables reproducible progress in historical and multilingual information extraction, guiding practitioners toward models robust to OCR noise, temporal reasoning, and cross-language variation—useful for digital humanities, biography extraction, and cultural analytics.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram showing the two relation types (at vs. isAt) with example timelines and text snippets.
World map overlay linking person icons to place icons to illustrate multilingual, geo-temporal associations.
Bar chart comparing baseline vs. participant system performance across languages and noise levels.
Annotated text sample highlighting OCR noise, entity mentions, and the annotated relation for quick interpretability.
paper_title: CLEF HIPE-2026: Evaluating Accurate and Efficient Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Texts
paper_authors: Juri Opitz, Corina Raclé, Emanuela Boros, Andrianos Michail, Matteo Romanello
